bibl.title: Dopamine Cells Respond to Predicted Events during Classical Conditioning: Evidence for Eligibility Traces in the Reward-Learning Network

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how the dopamine response moves from reward to predictive cue during learning, and whether the temporal difference algorithm can produce that time course
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether dopamine cells show the stepwise latency migration that published TD models predict, and if not, which parameter settings would reproduce what they do show
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: shows cue and reward responses coexist rather than trading off, then finds the pattern is reproduced only by long eligibility traces and a low learning rate - turning physiology into a constraint on the algorithm's parameters
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A long-lasting eligibility trace keeps the weights of an earlier sensory signal open to modification for many time steps, so the reward-driven prediction error can be assigned back to the cue in one step instead of migrating one time step per trial
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A very low learning rate combined with a high eligibility-trace decay makes each trial change the weights only slightly, so responses to the cue and to the predicted reward coexist for a prolonged period before the reward response is suppressed
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Sustained firing in reverberating circuits, or biochemical processes at the synapse, could hold the seconds-long eligibility trace the model requires
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: an eligibility trace keeps earlier time steps modifiable, so a cue several steps back can be updated in one trial instead of waiting for the error to migrate
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: with a low learning rate each trial moves the weights only slightly, which is what lets cue and reward responses coexist for hundreds of trials
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: under TD(0) the error must arrive one step earlier per trial, so reaching a cue k steps back takes at least k trials
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: candidate substrates for a seconds-long trace are reverberating circuits and synaptic biochemistry
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: long traces with slow learning is the combination machine learning already found to give early but stable learning, which may be why biology uses it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The fitted parameter values are not claimed to be fixed neural constants, since a different model structure could yield different best-fitting values.
span.note: what this limits: the fitted parameter values: OUR RESULTS SHOULD NOT BE UNDERSTOOD AS PROVIDING EXPLICIT FIXED VALUES FOR NEURAL TD LEARNING PARAMETERS, BECAUSE THE SPECIFIC VALUES ... MAY BE DIFFERENT IF DETAILS OF THE MODEL STRUCTURE WERE CHANGED
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The stimulus representation assumed by the model (serial compound) is not known to be how the brain represents stimuli for reward learning.
span.note: what this limits: the timing predictions in particular: IT IS NOT KNOWN HOW SENSORY STIMULI ARE REPRESENTED IN THE BRAIN FOR REWARD LEARNING
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the paper refuses the strong reading of its own result: these are not fixed values for neural parameters, because a different model structure would shift them
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - the values are a property of this model structure
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: how the brain represents stimuli in time is unknown; the serial compound representation is a convention inherited from earlier models
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1, with the convention named: WE FOLLOWED MANY PREVIOUS STUDIES IN USING A SERIAL COMPOUND REPRESENTATION OF CONDITIONED STIMULI
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the animals had already had hundreds of solenoid-reward pairings before recording, so the click was not a neutral event at the start of conditioning
span.note: what this limits: any reading of the click as a neutral cue: ANIMALS WERE THEREFORE EXPOSED TO HUNDREDS OF SOLENOID-REWARD PAIRINGS BY THE TIME THE RECORDINGS WERE MADE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the negative prediction error signal is small and hard to measure against an already low baseline rate
span.note: what this limits: the negative prediction-error signal: THE AMPLITUDE OF INHIBITIONS WAS SMALL, CONSISTENT WITH THE FACT THAT INHIBITORY RESPONSES CAN BE DIFFICULT TO DETECT AND QUANTIFY IN NEURONS THAT ALREADY HAVE A LOW BASELINE RATE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: 21 of 45 electrophysiologically plausible cells failed the pharmacological test and were discarded
span.note: what this limits: what a 'dopamine neuron' means here, and in every study that skips the drug test: FROM 45 NEURONS THAT WERE POSSIBLY DOPAMINERGIC ON ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL CRITERIA, 24 ... WERE CONFIRMED DA NEURONS BASED ON HAVING A CLEAR INHIBITORY RESPONSE TO DOPAMINE AGONIST DRUGS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The temporal difference algorithm and its prediction-error signal, taken from machine learning, are used as the model of midbrain dopamine cell activity.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the temporal difference algorithm, imported as a candidate account of what dopamine cells compute
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the century-old requirement that some trace of the cue survive until the reward arrives, here identified with the eligibility trace
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the known trade-off that high lambda with low alpha buys stable early learning, used here as an adaptive argument
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: electrode track positions confirmed histologically after the experiments were completed
span.note: eliminates: attributing the responses to dopamine cells that were not where the recordings were thought to be - the confirmation comes after, from the tissue, not from the coordinates
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: presumed DA cells are a doubly filtered category: rate below 10 Hz and spike at least 1 ms, THEN more than 50% inhibition by a dopamine agonist. Cell identity is pharmacological here, not genetic or anatomical
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: TD(0), TD(1) and TD(lambda) are three different models, not one - the value of lambda changes which weights an error can touch, and the published DA models were TD(0)
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: prediction error here is the scalar difference between actual reward and the temporal difference of successive predictions, with the NEGATIVE side deliberately clipped to match dopamine cells' floor
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: early and late training are defined by block count - 6 or fewer against 10 or more - and the paper's central result holds only early
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the recorded population pools substantia nigra pars compacta, ventral tegmental area and supramammillary nucleus, justified by a null on regional differences
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: builds-on → Montague et al. (1996) temporal-difference model of dopamine activity
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contradicts → previous TD models predicting a gradual stepwise latency shift (Montague et al., 1996; Schultz et al., 1997)
span.note: differs in: the time course of the latency shift: previous TD models PREDICT A GRADUAL STEPWISE SHIFT IN LATENCY WITH RESPONSES TO REWARDS LOST BEFORE RESPONSES DEVELOP TO THE CONDITIONED CUE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: extends → Miller et al., 1981; Kosobud et al., 1994; Kiyatkin and Rebec, 2001; Hyland et al., 2002 (rat DA cell responses to reward-predicting cues)
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contradicts → the stepwise latency migration predicted by TD(0) models of dopamine activity
span.note: differs in: the latency profile of the new response: NEW CONDITIONED RESPONSES MADE THEIR FIRST APPEARANCE AT A CONSTANT, SHORT LATENCY AFTER PREDICTIVE CUES, and DEVELOPED RAPIDLY, WITHIN A FEW TRIALS - not the gradual migration the models expect
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contradicts → the prediction that a redundant intermediate cue draws no response
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contradicts → the prediction that reward responses vanish before cue responses appear
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: reconciles → the temporal difference framework with the recorded time course, by relocating the disagreement to parameter choice
span.note: differs in: the model's free parameters: THESE APPARENT DISPARITIES BETWEEN TD MODEL PREDICTION ERRORS AND DA CELL ACTIVITY ARE ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE PARTICULAR CHOICE OF PARAMETERS USED IN THE MODEL - the settings for ALPHA and LAMBDA, not the framework
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critiques → published primate datasets, which on re-inspection never supported gradual migration either
span.note: differs in: gradual migration against simultaneous responding, and the stage of learning: the existing primate data PROVIDES NO SUPPORT FOR THE GRADUAL MIGRATION OF A RESPONSE DURING LEARNING AND SUGGESTS THAT DA CELLS SHOW SIMULTANEOUS RESPONDING TO BOTH CUE AND REWARD, AT LEAST EARLY IN LEARNING
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: confirms → earlier reports that reward responses are diminished in highly trained animals
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: extends → rat studies showing dopamine responses to reward-predicting cues, by showing they arise during acquisition
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Dopamine cells went on responding to the reward long after they had developed responses to the predictive cue, contradicting the prediction that the reward response dies before the cue response appears.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: New conditioned responses appeared straight away at their final short latency after the cue, with no gradual backward drift of latency from reward to cue.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Every cell trained with two cues in sequence responded clearly to the second, seemingly redundant cue, and that response persisted for the whole experiment.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Cells recorded after many sessions of cue-reward pairing no longer responded to a predictable reward, unlike the cells recorded early in training.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Acquiring a cue response and losing the reward response run on different time courses rather than being two sides of one shift.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Omitting an expected reward produced a significant drop in firing rate, whereas omitting the expected second cue did not differ significantly from baseline.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Leaving out the second cue restored the dopamine response to the reward up to the level seen when reward was delivered at random, both early and late in training.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Setting the eligibility-trace decay to 0.9 and the learning rate to 0.005 made the TD model reproduce the recorded dopamine pattern, including a time-locked response to the intermediate cue and coexisting cue and reward responses.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A high eligibility-trace decay parameter was the one setting that let the model learn cue significance without stepwise trial-by-trial migration of the response from reward to cue.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Once the eligibility-trace decay fell below about 0.6, stepwise migration of the prediction error reappeared no matter what learning rate was used.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: conditioned responses appeared at their final short latency within a few trials, with no gradual migration
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the redundant intermediate cue drew a clear response in every two-cue cell, which persisted
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: responses to predicted reward persisted after cue responses had developed, in every cell recorded early in training
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: after ten or more blocks the reward response was gone, so the two changes have different time courses
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: those late-training cells still responded to reward when it arrived uncued, so the loss is prediction-specific and not fatigue
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: omitting the second cue restored the reward response to its uncued level, so the redundant cue was doing predictive work
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: TD with eligibility zero and a fast learning rate reproduced the published pattern, with no second-cue response and no overlap
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: TD with lambda 0.9 and alpha 0.005 reproduced the recorded pattern, including the coexistence and the intermediate cue response
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: lambda below about 0.6 brought stepwise migration back for every value of alpha, making it the critical parameter
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: omitted rewards produced a significant firing decrease but omitted cues did not
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: CONTROL NULL: no regional difference in response pattern, which is what licensed pooling the three midbrain sites
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: BUILT IN, NOT PREDICTED: the model's small negative errors follow from the clipping imposed to match dopamine cells' floor, as the authors state
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: re-inspection of published primate datasets found no support for gradual migration there either
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
